title: They followed him.
paragraphs: But they were never meant to stay.

Imagine giving your whole life to prepare people for something…
only to watch them walk away from you the moment it finally arrives.

No applause.
No farewell speech.
No “thank you.”
Just silence… and disappearing footsteps in the water.
This is the tension of hidden obedience.
This is the wound of unrecognized faithfulness.
And if we’re honest… this is where pride starts to scream.
Because deep inside, we don’t just want to serve God.
We want to be seen doing it.
We say we want Jesus to be lifted high…
…but we still check if our name is mentioned.
…but we quietly hope we get the credit.

Pride vs surrender.
Platform vs obedience.
Recognition vs righteousness.
John the Baptist stood in that war… and chose to lose.

Lose the spotlight.
Lose the crowd.
Lose the attention.
“He must increase, but I must decrease.” — John 3:30

Some scholars interpret this not just as a statement of humility…
but as a declaration of identity.

Not the Christ.
Not the Savior.
Not the center.
“I am the voice of one crying out in the wilderness, ‘Make straight the way of the Lord.’” — John 1:23
And voices are meant to be heard… then fade.
Because pride doesn’t want to fade.
Pride wants applause that echoes long after the moment is over.
The Kingdom of God is not built on who is remembered by people…
…but on who is faithful before God.
You can serve God publicly… and still be driven by pride privately.
You can preach, lead, post, give, sacrifice…
Because pride competes with God for glory.
And God does not share His glory.
“I am the Lord; that is my name; my glory I give to no other.” — Isaiah 42:8
Because God is not exposing you to shame you…
He is exposing you to free you.
And here is the Gospel turn.
Because the real issue is not just pride.
And no amount of ministry, service, or sacrifice can erase it.
That’s why John pointed away from himself and cried:
“Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!” — John 1:29

Not your effort.
Not your humility performance.
Not your hidden obedience.
The Lamb who takes away sin.

Not manages it.
Not hides it.
Not negotiates with it.
On the cross, Jesus carried not just your obvious sins…
…but your secret need to be seen.

Your hidden pride that whispers,
“Notice me.”
And He didn’t just expose it.
“For our sake he made him to be sin who knew no sin, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.” — 2 Corinthians 5:21
You don’t have to fight for recognition.
You are already fully seen by God.
You don’t have to prove your worth.
You don’t have to build your name.
Jesus gave you a new one.
This is the freedom John understood.
So let me ask you, heart to heart:
or are you serving your need to be seen?
if your name was never mentioned?
This is where real surrender begins.
“Your Father who sees in secret will reward you.” — Matthew 6:4

Every hidden prayer.
Every quiet sacrifice.
Every unnoticed act of obedience.

The need to be recognized.
The hunger for applause.
The quiet competition for attention.
Lay it at the feet of Jesus.
Not just of what you’ve done…
Because the same Jesus John pointed to…
is the same Jesus reaching for you now.
To free you from the exhausting need to be seen.
It is enough that He sees.
Send this to someone who’s quietly serving and feels unseen.
